hints: Two phases with different constant accelerations. The second phase starts with the speed reached at burn-out.
worded:
1. Phase 1 (fuel on): from rest at 10 m/s² for 60 s, so speed 600 m/s and height ½ × 10 × 3600 = 18 km.

2. Phase 2 (fuel out): the rocket still moves up at 600 m/s but now decelerates at g = 10 m/s². It rises another 600²/20 = 18 km.

3. Maximum height 18 + 18 = 36 km. (D)

4. Symmetry check: the free phase has the same rate (10) as the powered phase, so it is a mirror image and covers the same height.
mistakes: The rocket doesn’t stop when the fuel runs out; it keeps rising (18 km alone is option A).
After burn-out the acceleration is g downward, not zero.
